sections.description:
SHARIAT BENCHES OF
SHARIAT BENCHES OF
SUPERIOR COURTS RULES, 1979.
In exercise of the powers
conferred by section 7 of the Constitution of Shariat Benches of Superior
Courts Ordinance, 1979, the Supreme Court, in consultation with the High Court,
is pleased to make the following Rules for the purposes of the Ordinance:‑
CHAPTER‑I
GENERAL
(1) Short title, extent and commencement.‑-- (1) These Rules
may be called the Shariat Benches of Superior Courts Rules, 1979.
(2) They shall apply to the whole
of Azad Jammu and Kashmir, in respect of the matters referred to in the
Ordinance.
(3) They shall come into force at
once.
2. Definitions.‑--- (1) In these Rules, unless the context
otherwise requires:‑
"Ordinance" means the
Constitution of Shariat Benches of Superior Courts Ordinance, 1979;
"Constitution" means
the Azad Jammu and Kashmir Interim Constitution Act, 1974;
"Government" means the
Azad Government of the State of Jammu and Kashmir.
(2) All words and expressions
used, but not defined in these rules, shall have the same meaning as in the
Constitution or the Ordinance, 1979.
(3) The General Clauses Act, 1897
(X of 1897) applies for the interpretation of these Rules as it applies for the
interpretation of an act of the Legislature.
CHAPTER‑II
PETITIONS
3. Particulars of petition.‑--- (1) Petition presented under
Section 4 of the Ordinance shall be self contained and in particular state:‑
(a) The name of the Shariat Bench in which it is filed
(b) The name description and address of the petitioner.
(c) That the petitioner is a citizen of Azad Jammu and Kashmir.
(d) The law, provision of law or a part thereof, which the
petitioner wants to get examined for
its repugnance to the injunctions of Islam.
(e) The grounds on which the petitioner considers the law to be repugnant
to the injunctions of Islam.
(2) The provisions of sub‑rule (1) shall apply, mutatis,
mutandis, to the petitions filed by
the Azad Jammu and Kashmir Government.
(3) In petitions filed by a citizen of Azad Jammu and Kashmir the
Government shall be impleaded
as a party depending upon its legislative competence in respect of the law sought to be examined.
4. Language of petition.‑ Unless otherwise permitted by
the Bench in exceptional cases, the
petition shall be made in quadruplicate and shall be legibly written or typed on one side of a thick foolscap
paper in the language of the Court. Petition to
be signed and certified.‑ (1) The petition shall be signed and certified
by the petitioner.
(2) The petition shall contain a certificate that a similar
petition was not made by the petitioner
before the same or any other Shariat Bench.
(3) Each copy of the petition shall be accompanied by:
(a) A list of books and authorities specifying pages to be cited;
and
(b) A list of the names of Ulema, experts, jurisconsults and
witnesses whom the petitioner
intends to produce before the Shariat Bench in support of his petition.
6. Presentation of
petition.‑ (1) Every petition shall be presented personally by the petitioner, a legal practitioner or a
jurisconsult, if any, to an officer of the Court nominated by the Chief Justice for this purpose during
Court hours on any working day.
(2) The officer on being
satisfied that the petition fulfils the requirements of this Chapter, shall
cause the petition to be registered in a Register entitled "Shariat
Petition" as given in the Schedule and inform the petitioner (and the
legal partitioner or jurisconsult if any) of the date when the petition shall
be taken up by the Shariat Bench for preliminary hearing and have it shown in a
cause list.
(3) Incomplete petition or
petitions not in conformity with the Ordinance or these Rules shall be returned
by the officer with objections in writing:
Provided that the petitioner may
request that the petition be referred to the Shariat Bench for orders.

HEARINGS
